There are three main "denominations" of Buddhism, each having its own perspective on the way to accomplish release from the cycle of rebirth (samsara). Hinayana ("small vehicle"), Mahayana ("great vehicle"), and Vajrayana ("thunderbolt vehicle") Buddhism represent the major subdivisions within Buddhism; each of these systems have additional subdivisions and varieties of thought and practices.

Theravada ("Wisdom of the Elders") is the most well-known community within the Hinayana school. This form of Buddhism is practiced throughout most of southeast Asia, with the exception of Vietnam. Theravadins work to eliminate cravings and ignorance through self-discipline. Theravada Buddhists practices are based on the idea that the Buddha was a human being that taught by example, and their prayer is to honor the Buddha, rather than to worship him. The model of enlightened life is the arhat, who primarily serves as an example for worshippers. All good acts done with the proper intent can work toward eradicating negative karma.

Mahayana Buddhism is pervasive in northeastern Asia - China, Korea, and Japan. Mahayana Buddhists believe that the Buddha was one of many manifestations of enlightenment. Unlike Theravada Buddhists, Mahayana Buddhist do not see the Buddha as only an ethical model, but as a representation of a universal presence and power. Instead of the exemplar of an arhat, Mahayana Buddhists aspire to become bodhisattvas - people who are able to reach Nirvana, but stay to help other beings. This idea is what gives rise to the name Mahayana - the idea that we are all in this together, and the salvation of one depends on the salvation of all.

Mahayana thought has given rise to the concept of "emptiness" as a way of emphasizing the futility of clinging to anything - even doctrine. Two particular schools of Mahayana Buddhism have become popular in northeastern Asia - Pure Land and Zen. Pure Land devotees believe they can be reborn into a heavenly paradise. Zen Buddhism emphasizes silent structured meditation.

Vajrayana Buddhism, common in the Himalayan region, incorporates Tantric thought and practices. There are several major orders within Vajrayana Buddhism, including Gelug-pa, which is headed by the Dalai Lama. Monasteries are common in the Vajrayana tradition, and Monks and nuns practice arcane rituals and have sacred texts. For example, the 225-volume Tanjur includes Sutras, Tantras and commentaries on them. The monks and nuns also minister to and teach the public. Visualization and chanting during meditation are common in Vajrayana Buddhism. These practices assist the practitioner in finding his divine center.

Manufacturers Description: “A unique favourite that offers a delicate blend of citrus, fruits and peppermint to bring a refreshing fruity and menthol bite.”

Packaging: 10ml bottle

Vaping stats: 3mg strength, vaped on a Mutation X V4 (0.8Ω dual-coil 28AWG Kanthal A1 – Japanese cotton wick) @ 50w

Review: NovaVapes are a small company with a specific ideal, which is stated on their website, “We offer premium tasting juice at a fraction of the cost”. I have tasted everything from my Aunties DIY-juice, to Petrol Station bought stank-juice, through vape-shop own brand, right up to the high tier (and high priced) premium brands. Although NovaVapes don’t quite hit the same heights as the super premium e-juices, it is still better than many of the juices made by the experienced blenders in vape shops, in my humble opinion. In contrast, enjoyably, is the price! This is considerably cheaper than any of the famous premium brands I have tried so far, and indeed, is cheaper than most vape shop own-brand juices. Considering it isn’t out of the ordinary to pay up to £10 for 15ml of premium brands (£0.66 per ml) or £4 for 10ml of vape shop own-brands (£0.40 per ml), this stuff comes in at an outrageously reasonable £6 for 30ml (£0.20 per ml). I feel this is a very important distinction, considering the crazy prices many of us pay for our favourite juices. With that in mind I’ll proceed to the important stuff: is it cheap and nasty, or cheap and tasty?

First off, I really like this stuff, especially considering the price; and if any of you reading this have perused my previous reviews you will notice I am not usually a fan of mint (or menthol) heavy flavours. The manufacture states that this is a citrus & fruit flavour with a peppermint bite without specifying which fruits exactly. If i had to call out a specific fruit flavour profile I would say blackcurrant, lemon/ lime and peppermint. It’s a great blend my friends. The peppermint is immediately prominent as soon as you hit the fire button and draw the clouds in, with a blackcurrant undertone tingling your taste buds on the way in. As soon as you start exhaling the fun really begins, the citrus stalks up the back of your throat like a hungry wolf and the blackcurrant forms a phalanx with the merciless intent of subjugating your taste buds for the empire. Which empire? Doesn’t matter. I want to be part of it… take my tithe and be done.

This is a candy-fruit flavour profile, rather than true-fruit. Sometimes this can be a little gaudy, and maybe not something you want to be blowing clouds of if you are having a sneaky vape in work (we all do it, let’s be honest here), as this fragrance will follow you, making it laughably obvious what you were up to. But after dinner, sitting up in front of the TV, you’ll be throwing out clouds to rival Mount Vesuvius; a characteristic of the high VG to PG ratio the manufacture defaults to (also worth knowing is that NovaVapes will make up any ratio of PG/VG that you ask for during your purchase).

Although I adore my premium juices, I tend to keep large bottles of my local vape store own-brand juice about to use in my Nautilus during my lunch in work, as Bill Gates I am not, according to my latest bank balance. I would end up spending an appalling amount of money every week on e-juice if that were the case, and I know I am not the only person who does this. With this in mind I will be using NovaVapes juices in lieu of the more expensive and cheaper tasting own-brand stuff from now on. The prices are scandalously good, and the flavour is pretty damn good too.

Flavour: 7 / 10

Affordability: ~£0.20 per ml (at time of writing)
